idiom_name: Promise.allSettled over a computed recipient array
implementation_notes: The router collapses into a resolved array plus one combinator: await Promise.allSettled(recipients.map(r => deliver(r, copy))) performs the traversal, and allSettled is the right primitive because it never short-circuits - it returns one outcome per recipient, matching the pattern's copy-to-everyone semantics instead of losing the remaining sends to the first rejection. Broker clients (amqplib, kafkajs, BullMQ) add durability and retries, but the recipient set stays application data either way. Classic router classes are only worth it when retry policy, allow-lists or throttling must be shared across call sites.
pitfalls: Promise.all() short-circuits on the first rejection, so the caller sees one failure while the other deliveries are still in flight; allSettled is the combinator this pattern wants.
Handing the same object reference to every recipient lets any handler in-process mutate the payload for the others (or for a retry); clone per recipient.
All recipients settle at once with no concurrency limit, so a large list opens as many sockets or HTTP requests as it has entries; use a limiter such as p-limit.
